problem:
A linear transformation $T$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis. Given that $u=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $T(u)=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix of $T?$

|  |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $T=\,\,$ |  |  |  |  |
|  |  | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |  |
worked_solution:
First, we are told that $T$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis.

Comparing the $x$- and $y$-components of $u$ and $T(u),$ we note the following:

- the $x$-components of $u$ and $T(u)$ are the same, while

- the $y$-component of $T(u)$ is $\sqrt{3}$ times the $y$-component of $u.$

So, we conclude that $T$ represents a stretch of scale factor $\sqrt{3}$ in the $y$-direction. 

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}].
$$
